content.metaDescription: Give your hallway or living room serious old-money style with these vintage world map prints — classic black and grey tones, timeless explorer appeal. Free UK shipping!
content.productDescription:
Hang these world map prints in your hallway or living room and you'll immediately get that quietly confident, old-money feel that's so hard to put your finger on but so easy to love. One print features a beautifully detailed antique world globe sitting on a dark turned-wood base, rendered in rich black and soft grey tones — the kind of thing you'd find in a well-travelled gentleman's study. The companion print is a close-up, dramatic angle of a vintage astronomical or navigational instrument — think engraved arcs, fine scale markings, and ornate scroll details, all shot in the same striking monochrome palette. Together they feel considered, intelligent, and genuinely stylish.

What I really like about this pair is how effortlessly masculine and classic they feel without being cold or stuffy. The deep blacks and warm mid-greys give them real presence on the wall, and because both prints share that same vintage, explorer-era spirit, they sit together as though they were always meant to be a set. If you're after something with a bit of character and substance — not just pretty decoration — this could be exactly what you're looking for.

What's Included with Vintage World Map Prints | Antique Globe & Sundial Black and Grey Art | Set of 2

  • A set of 2 art prints: one antique world globe print and one vintage navigational instrument print, both in a classic black and grey colour palette
  • Printed in the UK using fade-resistant pigment inks, designed for indoor display
  • The framed and canvas-wrapped options arrive ready to hang — no need to hunt for a frame that fits, saving you time and hassle
  • Choose between unframed and framed options in multiple sizes and in Luster or Museum quality; also available in wrapped canvas size options

How to Style World Map Prints in Your Home

My go-to for a pair like this is a hallway — hang them side by side at eye level with an even gap between them, and they immediately set the tone the moment anyone walks through the door. Because both prints are monochrome, they work brilliantly against warm white, deep charcoal, or dark navy walls — the contrast really lets those fine engraved details sing. If you want to lean into the old-money, classic-study look, try pairing them with dark wood furniture, leather accessories, or a simple brass wall light nearby. None of that needs to be expensive; it's all about the combination.

In a living room they're equally at home above a console table, a fireplace, or a bookcase — anywhere you want to add a layer of quiet sophistication. I'd keep the surrounding decor fairly restrained so the prints do the talking. For more inspiration on putting together a classic, masculine space, have a browse through our black and white wall art collection — there are some lovely pieces that would sit well alongside this set.

Choosing the Right Size and Finish for These Prints

Because both prints carry a good amount of fine detail — the engraved scales and lettering on the instrument print, and the cartographic linework on the globe — I'd always suggest going as large as your wall comfortably allows. A larger size really lets you appreciate all of that intricate vintage character up close. If you're working with a narrower hallway wall, a medium size hung vertically still looks smart and intentional.

For finish, Museum quality paper gives you exceptional depth and sharpness, which suits the fine monochrome detail in these prints beautifully. Luster paper is a brilliant choice if you want a subtle sheen that makes the black tones feel richer — both are great, it really comes down to personal preference. If you'd prefer something with even more impact, the wrapped canvas option gives these prints a real gallery feel with no framing needed at all.

Scroll down to see how each size looks in a hallway before you decide — there's a size-guide image below showing every option in that room so you can picture exactly how it'll look on your wall.

What are world map prints?

World map prints are decorative art prints featuring maps, globes, or geographic imagery, designed to be displayed on your walls as a stylish and meaningful focal point. They range from bold contemporary designs to detailed vintage and antique-style illustrations, making them one of the most versatile choices in home decor. A classic world map print brings a sense of adventure, curiosity, and timeless sophistication to any room — from a hallway to a home office or living room. They work especially well in sets, where two or more complementary prints create a cohesive, gallery-style display that feels intentional and put-together.

How to Hang World Map Prints as a Pair

1. Choose your wall space: Find a wall with enough width to display both prints side by side with a small, even gap between them — around 5 to 10 cm works well for most sizes. A hallway wall, the space above a console table, or a chimney breast are all great spots.

2. Find the right height: Hang the centre of your prints at roughly eye level — around 145 to 150 cm from the floor to the centre of each print is a good general rule. If you're hanging them above a piece of furniture, aim for the bottom edge of the prints to sit around 15 to 20 cm above it.

3. Mark your positions before committing: Use a pencil and a spirit level to mark where each hanging point will go. Cut out paper templates in your print sizes and stick them to the wall with masking tape first — this lets you adjust the layout without making extra holes.

4. Hang and check alignment: Once your prints are up, step back and check they are level and evenly spaced. A small spirit level placed on top of each print is the quickest way to make sure everything sits straight.

Which Format is Right for Your World Map Prints?

Format — Unframed print: the print only, ready for you to frame as you like. Framed print: arrives ready to hang with no extra shopping needed. Wrapped canvas: a gallery-style canvas with no frame or glazing required.

Ready to hang — Unframed print: No (you choose your own frame). Framed print: Yes, straight out of the box. Wrapped canvas: Yes, with no frame needed at all.

Paper / surface choice — Unframed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Framed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Wrapped canvas: Canvas wrap (no paper options).

Best for — Unframed print: Those who already have a frame in mind or want full control over the look. Framed print: Anyone who wants a complete, polished result with minimal effort. Wrapped canvas: A contemporary, gallery-wall feel with real depth and texture.

Suits this set — Unframed print: Great if you want to match existing dark or natural wood frames. Framed print: Perfect for a sharp, classic monochrome display. Wrapped canvas: Ideal for a bold, statement look in a living room or hallway.
